newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France Europe executive resigns.
newsitem.headline: Air France Europe executive resigns.

text.p: The managing director of Air France Europe, the domestic and regional unit of the Air France group, has handed in his notice of resignation, the airline said on Tuesday.

Jean-Pierre Courcol said in a letter to Air France Europe employees that he would leave the company in the next few days as the task handed to him of creating a European airline would end with the creation of the new merged Air France and Air France Europe companies.

"The terrible economic war being waged between the leading world airlines and the current situation of Air France Europe...have convinced me that the merger has become the only way to maintain jobs and to complete the restructuring that I conceived and finalised with the company's management team," Courcol write in his letter.
"Thus, the mission that Christian Blanc gave me to create the European company, a year ago, will end at the same time as the birth of the new French company," he said.
Air France Europe pilots blocked moves to create a separate European company, forcing a merger with parent Air France.
Blanc hired Courcol last year, following resignation of the previous Air France Europe chairman Michael Bernard who was thwarted by employees who opposed his restructuring plan.
The consultative employee committee of Air France Europe, formerly Air Inter, on Monday rejected the current recovery plan, which includes shedding some 950 jobs out of 11,000 over two years.
The merger is due to take place next year and is part of a plan to bring Air France Europe back to break even within two years, and includes axing loss-making routes and launching a shuttle service.
